findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The inspector observed the following non food contact surfaces of equipment to have accumulated soil: The Nestle glass top ice cream freezer (frost), the bottom of Dairy cooler in back stock, bottom of Dairy cooler in store, bottom of cold drink cooler under milk in store. Clean and maintain these areas clean for the next routine inspection. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
5-501.15: (A) Receptacles for REFUSE used outside shall be designed and constructed to have tight-fitting lids, doors, or covers. (B) Receptacles for REFUSE shall be installed so debris and insect and rodent attraction are minimized. 

Inspector observed blowing litter and debris in the grassy area behind and to the West of the store. Rolltainers, open rolling containers that hold refuse and recyclables, are stored outside of the building just outside of the receiving door. Corporate requires that they be stored outside so that they do not block the exit or pose a fire hazard. The facility manager states that they have been fighting with this issue for approximately 3 to 6 months. Manager states that drivers do not remove the rolltainers as they are required to by corporate policy. The truck delivered this morning and did not remove any rolltainers. This initiated a ticket for service, #DG18147231003001, rolltainer sweep,  to be put in by the manager.  She also stated that they have looked into placing a barricade fence or some type of fence in order to corral the rolltainers and blowing litter. It is her understanding that the request to build a fence was denied by the village.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple reach-in cold holding units to lack thermometers. Ensure all cold holding units have thermometers to gauge air temperature in the unit. Purchase before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15  (Pf) Cans are dented and in poor condition. Food packaging must be in good condition so that foods are not exposed to adulteration or potential contamination. Reference 3-202.15.

Observed several dented cans on shelving units throughout store. Inspector pulled the cans and facility voluntarily put in back room. Discussed with PIC that cans should not be received if in heavily dented condition. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of ice cream chest freezer is no longer easily cleanable. Reference 4-101.19.

Observed customer ice cream chest freezer to be heavily accumulated with frost. Discussed routine cleaning of chest freezer with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on bottom shelves of all reach-in cold holding units. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed accumulation of food debris and soil residue on all cold holding customer reach-in units of facility. Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13  (P) Waste water from mop bucket is being improperly disposed. All sewage discharge must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Reference 5-402.13.

Observed waste water from mop bucket to be within bucket and not disposed of in-betwen uses. Discussed proper mop water disposal with PIC. COS.
